q: What is the best lighting to highlight a painting?
n: A spotlight (adjustable accent light) throws a focused beam on the painting, making it stand out from the surroundings. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (accent lighting).

q: What lighting is best for a workspace or reading area?
n: Task lighting puts concentrated light on the work or reading surface, at higher illuminance than the room's general light. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; Philippine Green Building Code lighting guidance.

q: Which wall-mounted fixture gives both decorative and functional light?
n: A sconce is a wall-mounted fixture that gives decorative appeal and useful up- or down-light. Source: IES Lighting Handbook; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which lighting emphasizes architectural features, art or displays?
n: Accent lighting creates contrast on a focal point, such as artwork, textures or displays, typically at three times or more the surrounding brightness. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: Which lighting creates a warm, inviting feel in a living room?
n: Ambient (general) lighting gives soft, even illumination that sets a warm, inviting mood in living rooms, usually at warm color temperatures. Source: IES Lighting Handbook.

q: What general term covers particle board, fiberboard and gypsum board?
n: Wallboard is the general term for large prefabricated sheets used to finish walls and ceilings, including gypsum, particle and fiber boards. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Fiber cement board is mainly cement, cellulose fiber and ______.
n: Fiber cement board is made of portland cement, cellulose fibers and finely ground silica sand, autoclaved for strength and stability. Source: ASTM C1186 (flat fiber cement sheets); James Hardie product literature.

q: Which material is good for ceilings because it absorbs sound?
n: Gypsum board ceilings, especially perforated or with an insulation backing, absorb and dampen sound well and are light and fire-resistant. Source: Gypsum Association; manufacturer acoustic data.

q: What is the standard size of a marine plywood sheet?
n: Plywood, including marine plywood, comes in standard 4 ft × 8 ft (1.22 m × 2.44 m) sheets, written as 1.20 m × 2.40 m. Source: PS 1 Structural Plywood standard; Philippine lumber supplier catalogs.

q: What is the standard thickness of gypsum board for wall partitions?
n: 12 mm (1/2 in.) gypsum board is the standard thickness for wall partitions. 9 mm is used for ceilings and 15–16 mm Type X for fire-rated walls. Source: ASTM C1396 (gypsum board); Gypsum Association GA-600.

q: What is placed between two surfaces to stop gas, oil or other substances passing through?
n: A sealant, or a gasket, is applied in the joint between two surfaces to close it against the passage of gas, liquids, water and dust. Putty is a glazing compound and mortar binds masonry. Source: ASTM C920 (elastomeric joint sealants); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which of the following materials has the greatest embodied energy?
o: Tooled finish for a concrete wall
n: High-gloss glazed wall tiles are fired at high temperature, often twice, and glazed, so they carry far more embodied energy than unfired or simply tooled materials like a concrete finish, crazy-cut stone or common brick. Source: University of Bath ICE (Inventory of Carbon and Energy) database.

q: Which material has the lowest embodied carbon per kilogram before delivery to site?
n: Per kilogram, steel (especially with recycled content) has much lower embodied carbon than primary aluminum, copper or plastics, which need very energy-intensive smelting or petrochemical processing. Source: University of Bath ICE database.

q: What type of road pavement least allows water to percolate?
n: Dense asphalt pavement is practically impermeable, so rainwater runs off it. Sand and open aggregate let water percolate, and concrete can be made pervious. Source: US EPA, Stormwater Best Management Practices (pervious pavement).

q: Which paver best reduces outdoor heat gain and helps keep interiors cool?
n: Light-colored, unglazed (matte) white tiles have high solar reflectance, so the paving absorbs less sun, stays cooler and reduces the heat radiated toward the building. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), heat island mitigation; US EPA Heat Island guidelines.

q: What flooring material is best for a fast-food restaurant?
n: Vitrified tiles are dense and almost non-porous, with absorption under 0.5%. They resist stains, grease and heavy foot traffic and are easy to clean, which suits fast-food kitchens and dining areas. Source: ISO 13006 / ANSI A137.1 (porcelain tile classification).

q: What flooring material is most suitable for a retrofitted office space with a plywood subfloor?
n: Vinyl tile is light and flexible, so it can be laid on a plywood subfloor in a retrofit without the rigid, heavy mortar bed and crack-isolation that ceramic tile needs. Source: Resilient Floor Covering Institute installation guidelines; TCNA Handbook.

q: Which flooring becomes slippery when dusty?
n: Polished granite has a very smooth, hard surface. A film of dust acts like ball bearings on it, so it becomes slippery. Textured vinyl, rubber and unglazed ceramic keep their grip. Source: ANSI A326.3 (dynamic coefficient of friction); Natural Stone Institute.

q: What is commonly used as underlayment for wood flooring?
n: Floating wood and laminate floors are laid over a thin foam underlayment that cushions, levels minor bumps, reduces footfall noise and acts as a moisture barrier. Source: NWFA Installation Guidelines; flooring manufacturer literature.

q: Which is the cheapest flooring option among the choices?
n: Ordinary ceramic tile is the cheapest per square meter of the options. Vinyl plank, engineered wood and plastic laminate generally cost more. Source: Philippine construction cost references; local supplier price lists.

q: Ceiling commonly used for restaurants and bars:
n: Restaurants and bars are noisy, so acoustic ceiling panels are used to absorb sound and keep conversation intelligible. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (restaurants); Egan, Architectural Acoustics.

q: Ceiling commonly used for warehouses:
n: Warehouses are usually left with no ceiling: the roof framing is exposed, giving maximum clear height for racking and easy access to lights and sprinklers. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (warehouses).

q: Ceiling commonly used for a conference room:
n: Conference rooms commonly use a flat ceiling, which gives even lighting, simple integration of fixtures, projectors and diffusers, and predictable acoustics. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (offices).

q: Which flooring material is best for areas with light equipment?
n: Vinyl composition tile (VCT) is hard-wearing and resists rolling loads from light equipment and carts, and damaged tiles can be replaced individually. Sheet vinyl and laminate gouge more easily. Source: Resilient Floor Covering Institute; ASTM F1066 (VCT).

q: Engineered wood is purchased per__.
n: Engineered wood flooring is sold by the box, which holds a stated coverage, e.g. 1.5–2.5 m². Quantities are ordered in whole boxes. Source: Flooring manufacturer product literature.

q: How do you find the number of 60 × 120 cm acoustic boards for a ceiling?
n: One 0.60 × 1.20 m board covers 0.72 m², so the number of boards = ceiling area ÷ 0.72 (then add waste). Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (area method).

q: How many 60 × 60 cm acoustic tiles cover a 20 m × 30 m ceiling?
n: Area = 20 × 30 = 600 m². One tile = 0.6 × 0.6 = 0.36 m². 600 ÷ 0.36 = 1,666.7, so about 1,670 tiles. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (area method).

q: How many 1.2 × 2.4 m plywood sheets are needed for a 5 m × 7 m bedroom ceiling?
n: Area = 5 × 7 = 35 m². One sheet = 1.2 × 2.4 = 2.88 m². 35 ÷ 2.88 = 12.15, rounded up to 13 sheets. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (area method).

q: How many 300 × 300 mm tiles should be ordered for a 150 m² public toilet floor?
n: One 0.30 × 0.30 m tile = 0.09 m². 150 ÷ 0.09 = 1,667 tiles; with rounding for cuts and waste, order about 1,700 pieces. Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (area method).

q: How many 100 × 150 mm pavers cover 1 m²?
n: One paver = 0.10 × 0.15 = 0.015 m². 1 ÷ 0.015 = 66.7, and only whole pieces can be laid, so 67 pavers per m². Source: Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (area method).
